items.title: Marty Sheller interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 9, 2022
items.q: I was lucky enough to have had those two fellas as my teachers. ... Frankie would have me come to his house. ... he would play on my knees what he would play as a conga player, and explain why.

ctx.x: You mentioned the Miles Davis that you put away for a year and then you got it out again and you literally had a “bing.” Did you have to have a bing with absorbing the Latin rhythms and sort of getting it inside you?

In a way yes. ‘Cause that first gig that I mentioned to you where it was just a quartet playing Tito Puente arrangements, I couldn’t understand at the very beginning in Latin music the bass player does not play on the one, and that’s all the music I ever heard, the bass always played on the one. But on Latin music they play on the one and — one two three four one two boom bing, boom boom. That kind of rhythm. And I remember playing the first couple of songs and I was really thrown off, I was reading the music but…

that was my introduction to that end of the music. And like I said, I was always asking questions to make sure I knew exactly that I was getting the real deal, and I was lucky enough to have had those two fellas as my teachers.
